title: Two Bengaluru Sisters Turned Their Grandmother's Biryani Into a 28-Outlet Empire
excerpt: Ramya and Shweta Ravi launched RNR Donne Biryani from a 200 sq ft cloud kitchen during the pandemic with Rs 5 lakh. Five years later, they have 28 locations and are expanding to Chennai.
body:
• Sisters Ramya and Shweta Ravi started RNR Donne Biryani in November 2020 with just Rs 5 lakh from a 200 sq ft cloud kitchen in Bengaluru.
  • The brand has grown to 28 locations across Bengaluru and plans to expand to Chennai this year, with ambitions for pan-India and international markets.
  • RNR's distinctive triangle-shaped tin box packaging — where they spend over 10% of product cost vs the industry's 5% — drove organic social media buzz without paid influencer campaigns.
  • Donne biryani, a coriander-forward Karnataka variety served in leaf pouches, has gone from street-food obscurity to five-star restaurant menus thanks in part to RNR's efforts.

When Ramya Ravi and her sister Shweta decided to launch a biryani delivery brand from a cramped cloud kitchen in Nagarbhavi during the peak of the Covid-19 pandemic, the odds were not in their favour. Restaurants across Bengaluru were shutting down, and the hospitality industry was reeling.

But the sisters, raised in a family of restaurateurs, saw an opening. Donne biryani — Karnataka's signature rice dish served in leaf pouches, made with short-grain Jeeraga Samba rice and a vibrant green coriander base — was loved locally but had no organised brand behind it. Hyderabadi and Lucknowi biryani had national recognition. Donne biryani did not.

"During the pandemic, everyone was looking at the safety aspect when it came to food. We found a big gap when it came to donne biryani and decided to take a leap of faith."

— Ramya Ravi, Co-founder, RNR Donne Biryani

From Cloud Kitchen to City-Wide Chain

RNR Donne Biryani launched in November 2020 with an initial investment of Rs 5 lakh, a single cook, and a couple of assistants. The name honours the family — R for grandfather Ramaswamy, R for father Ravichandar — and the recipe is their grandmother's, unchanged for over 60 years.

The response was immediate: 10,000 orders in the first month. Delivery app Swiggy named RNR the best new brand for 2020. By March 2022, barely a year and a half after launch, the brand had crossed Rs 10 crore in revenue.

Much of that early traction came not from advertising, but from a box. RNR's triangle-shaped tin packaging — complete with raita, salad, and a sweet — was designed to be "social media-worthy," according to Ramya. Where the industry standard allocates roughly 5% of product cost to packaging, RNR spent over 10%.

"There are two kinds of marketing — push and pull. We chose pull marketing. We didn't onboard influencers initially. Instead, we focused on making our product so unique that it would create its own hype."

— Ramya Ravi, Co-founder, RNR Donne Biryani

What Makes Donne Biryani Different

Unlike its more famous cousins — the layered Hyderabadi dum biryani or the subtler Lucknowi variant — donne biryani has a distinctly Karnataka identity. The dish gets its vivid green colour from generous amounts of coriander and mint, uses short-grain Jeeraga Samba rice instead of long-grain basmati, and is traditionally served in "donne," cup-shaped pouches made from areca palm leaves.

It is a fixture of Karnataka's food culture, particularly in Bengaluru's street food scene, but had never been commercialised at scale before RNR. "While the donne biryani is available in Bengaluru, I always wondered why it wasn't as popular as the other types," Ramya told The Better India.

28 Outlets and Counting

Five years after that first cloud kitchen, RNR has expanded to 28 locations across Bengaluru, including stand-alone restaurants alongside its original cloud kitchen model. The menu has broadened too — drumstick chilli, chicken ghee roast, mutton nalli fry, and Elaneer payasam now sit alongside the flagship biryani.

Ramya handles operations while Shweta manages marketing. Their father, a veteran of the restaurant industry, operates in a different vertical. The division is deliberate. "We've made things simple by dividing our responsibilities clearly," Ramya says.

The brand is now preparing for its first expansion outside Bengaluru. "We've almost maximised our presence in Bengaluru. Now is the right time to enter another city — and yes, this year, we'll be launching in Chennai," Ramya confirmed in a recent interview with The Weekend Leader.

Shaping a Cuisine

Beyond revenue, Ramya points to a cultural shift as RNR's biggest win. "Five years ago, Donne Biryani wasn't being served in five-star hotels or upscale restaurants. Today, it is," she says. That transformation — from a hyperlocal street food to a cuisine with mainstream recognition — has been driven partly by RNR's branding and partly by broader interest in regional Indian food.

As the brand looks ahead to Chennai and potentially international markets, the focus remains on consistency. "Our goal was to make the recipe process-driven and not people-dependent. That's the only way to maintain quality as we scale," Ramya says. For a venture that began in a 200 sq ft kitchen during a global crisis, RNR's trajectory suggests the donne biryani's moment may have arrived.
image_caption: Ramya Ravi, co-founder of RNR Donne Biryani, at one of the brand's Bengaluru outlets. The sisters have expanded their grandmother's recipe into a 28-location chain across the city.
nri_angle: The story introduces NRIs to donne biryani — a lesser-known Karnataka variety most diaspora Indians haven't encountered — and showcases women-led food entrepreneurship in India.
